title: Longest Block With an Even Number of Each Vowel

concept.title: Parity of five counters packed into one number
body: You want a block in which each of the vowels `a e i o u` occurs an **even** number of times (zero counts as even). Only the **parity** (even or odd) of each count matters, so five yes/no values describe a prefix completely. Pack them into a 5-bit number, a **bitmask**: bit `j` is 1 when the vowel number `j` has occurred an odd number of times so far.

A block between two prefixes has all vowel counts even exactly when the two prefixes have the **same mask**. So store the **first position of every mask** (there are only 32 masks) and measure the distance when a mask appears again. Start with the empty prefix: mask 0 at position -1.

statement: Find the length of the longest block of consecutive letters of a word in which each of the vowels a, e, i, o and u appears an even number of times (a vowel that does not appear is fine, because 0 is even).
inputFormat: A single word of lowercase letters.

examples.note: The block leetminicowor has the vowels e, i and o twice each (a and u not at all): length 13.

hints: Only the parity of the count of each vowel matters.
Represent the five parities as a bitmask and flip a bit when a vowel is read.
Two prefixes with the same mask enclose a good block; store the first position of every mask.

explanation: The parities of the five vowel counts form a 5-bit mask. Two prefixes with equal masks enclose a block with all counts even; the first position of every mask gives the longest block.
